Batch 71 Forensic Discoveries

Batch 71 recovers and dates 14 rare historical recordings spanning Roaring Twenties and early Depression dance bands, late 1930s aviation cliffhangers, Native American oral traditions, 1970s paranormal documentary dramas, and Manhattan newspaper columnist mysteries: 5 vintage 78rpm transcriptions from Ben Selvin and His Orchestra (1929–1933, featuring seminal fox trots and Broadway melodies), 4 high-flying adventure chapters from Howie Wing, A Saga of Aviation (CBS, November–December 1938, sponsored by Kellogg's Corn Flakes), 2 folklore broadcasts from Chief Grey Wolf's Teepee (1949), 2 investigative episodes from Files of the Unknown (1974, uncovering the medieval mystery of the Green Children of Woolpit), and Manhattan columnist drama on The Adventures of Frank Farrell (1950).

1. Ben Selvin and His Orchestra — 1929–1933 Dance Band Transcriptions

Led by the legendary Columbia recording director and prolific dance band maestro:
